items.title: Roborock Saros 20 Neo è il robot aspirapolvere lavapavimenti che toglie di mezzo anche gli imprevisti
items.summary: Tanta automazione, stazione multifunzione e aspirazione da 36.000 Pa. Perché la vera innovazione è dover fare meno per la pulizia ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
I robot aspirapolvere hanno già risolto da tempo il problema più semplice: muoversi per casa raccogliendo polvere e sporco. Ciò che continua a fare la differenza, soprattutto nella fascia più alta del mercato, è tutto ciò che accade quando la casa smette di essere un ambiente ideale.

In pratica, quando ci sono i vari, piccoli ostacoli che sono comuni in un’abitazione normale: come un tappeto più spesso di un altro, una soglia alta o un cavo lasciato a terra. Oppure, semplicemente, la necessità di lavare e asciugare i mop senza che qualcuno debba intervenire ogni volta.

Roborock Saros 20 Neo è un robot che abbina 36.000 Pa di aspirazione a una serie di soluzioni pensate soprattutto per ridurre le situazioni nelle quali l’utente è costretto a preparare la casa prima della pulizia o a intervenire durante il ciclo. In altre parole, è un robot pensato per occuparsi anche degli imprevisti.

Ma c'è un altro motivo: Saros 20 Neo è in sconto a 749 euro su Amazon e sull'eshop di Roborock.

Uno dei limiti più evidenti dei robot aspirapolvere emerge quando incontrano dislivelli, soglie e tappeti. Per superarli, Saros 20 Neo utilizza il sistema AdaptiLift 3.0, progettato per modificare l’assetto del robot in base a ciò che trova davanti a sé. Nell’attività di pulizia permette quindi di superare soglie doppie alte complessivamente fino a 8,8 centimetri , suddivise in due passaggi da 4,5 e 4,3 centimetri. Il sistema è stato progettato per resistere a oltre 20.000 attraversamenti delle soglie, che equivalgono ad anni di pulizia quotidiana.

In più, Saros 20 Neo può sollevare il proprio assetto e gestire tappeti con pelo fino a 3 centimetri . Quando invece il lavaggio rischierebbe di rappresentare un problema oppure si è deciso di aspirare prima i tappeti attraverso l’apposita funzione, i mop vengono rimossi automaticamente quando il robot parte dalla base multifunzione, evitando così di trascinare superfici bagnate sopra i tappeti. Invece attivando la modalità di pulizia profonda dei tappeti, la spazzola principale del Saros 20 Neo rimane in posizione stabile verso il basso durante una seconda passata, per migliorare la raccolta dei detriti rispetto alla normale posizione flottante.

La potenza di aspirazione HyperForce raggiunge i 36.000 Pa , perfetta per aspirare lo sporco anche negli angoli, anche grazie all’inclusione del braccio laterale FlexiArm Arc può estendersi verso l’esterno per raggiungere più facilmente i bordi. A ciò si aggiunge il sistema Dual Anti-Tangle, che lavora insieme alla spazzola DuoDivide per limitare l’accumulo di capelli e peli. Insomma: Saros 20 Neo lascia il pavimento pulito e ordinato e poi non c’è bisogno di perdere tempo a rimuovere i capelli rimasti avvolti nella spazzola.

Per il lavaggio, Saros 20 Neo utilizza due mop rotanti che possono raggiungere una velocità di 200 giri al minuto e applicare fino a 14 N di pressione sul pavimento. Inoltre, Saros 20 Neo riduce fino al 30% l’acqua residua lasciata sul pavimento.

Prima ancora di aspirare o lavare, il robot deve capire che cosa ha davanti. Saros 20 Neo utilizza il sistema Reactive AI Obstacle Recognition, basato su fotocamera RGB e luce strutturata, insieme alla tecnologia VertiBeam.

Grazie a questo sistema avanzato, può riconoscere oggetti comuni che possono trovarsi sul pavimento, come cavi, scarpe, giocattoli, ciotole e altri piccoli ostacoli.

Per anni, uno dei consigli più comuni prima di avviare un robot aspirapolvere è stato togliere da terra tutto ciò che potrebbe confonderlo. Un prodotto come Saros 20 Neo ribalta invece il problema: è il robot che deve imparare a gestire ciò che trova; e il Saros 20 Neo ci riesce molto bene.

Allo scopo di adattare il robot alle esigenze domestiche e non viceversa, Saros 20 Neo misura 7,98 centimetri in altezza. Può sembrare una caratteristica meno evidente e impattante rispetto ai 36.000 Pa di aspirazione, ma le sue dimensioni gli permettono di passare facilmente sotto ai divani e ai letti oltre che sotto i mobili bassi fino a 7,95 cm, che spesso sono fra le zone più complicate per i robot dotati di torrette di navigazione più alte.

Saros 20 Neo ci riesce perché il sistema di scansione dell’ambiente circostante, che normalmente è sollevato per garantire una mappatura precisa, viene automaticamente ritratto e passa a una visuale posteriore a 100°: così il robot continua a sapere come muoversi ma può passare anche in spazi dove altri dispositivi non arrivano.

Ancora più interessante è il modo in cui il robot gestisce la differenza fra una stanza e l’altra. Con SmartPlan 3.0, Saros 20 Neo può adattare il ciclo di pulizia tenendo conto della tipologia di ambiente , dei materiali e dello storico delle sessioni precedenti. Per esempio, può intensificare la pulizia nelle aree che sono state trascurate oppure tornare alla base per lavare nuovamente i mop dopo essere passato in cucina o in bagno.

Inoltre, il Saros 20 Neo sa occuparsi anche di zone della casa che normalmente rischiano di essere trascurate. Contrassegnando manualmente le tende, per esempio, pulisce dietro tende e divisori morbidi, coprendo quindi anche le aree nascosto senza bisogno di sollevarli o regolarli. E quando le porte di una stanza sono chiuse, il Saros 20 Neo prosegue senza urtarle né spingerle, per evitare il rischio di danneggiarle. E se in precedenza ha evitato una zona - magari perché c’era un ostacolo temporaneo o un animale domestico - il sistema è progettato per proseguire l’attività di pulizia altrove e poi ritorna sulla zona non coperta appena è libera. Per di più, SmartPlan 3.0 è un sistema che continua a imparare dalle abitudini di pulizia e quindi migliora nel tempo.

Non è solo il robot a essere dotato di grande autonomia, perché anche la base multifunzione riesce a compiere tante operazioni senza bisogno di intervento. La base multifunzione infatti può svuotare automaticamente il contenitore della polvere, lavare i mop con acqua fino a 100 °C (rimuovendo il 99,99% dei batteri) e asciugarli successivamente con aria calda fino a 55 °C.

Il sistema può anche rilevare il livello di sporco dei mop e decidere di prolungarne il lavaggio oppure richiedere al robot un ulteriore passaggio nell’area appena pulita. Sono previste anche il riempimento automatico con acqua calda e il dosaggio del detergente.

La parte interna della base è rimovibile, così da semplificarne la pulizia quando necessario. È forse qui che si vede meglio il cambiamento avvenuto in questa categoria di prodotti.

Una parte della gestione rimane comunque nelle mani dell’utente. Attraverso l’app Roborock è possibile lavorare sulle mappe, dividere gli ambienti, creare zone escluse, scegliere modalità e intensità della pulizia oppure definire il comportamento sui tappeti.

Anche i comandi vocali possono essere utilizzati direttamente attraverso "Hello Rocky" , anche senza Wi-Fi, che permette di avviare o interrompere la pulizia, indicare una stanza, localizzare il robot oppure modificare aspirazione e quantità d’acqua. Il sistema può funzionare anche offline. Inoltre, supporta il protocollo Matter, che consente di automatizzare le routine e controllare i vari dispositivi della smart home da un’unica piattaforma, che sia Alexa, Siri o Google Home.

items.title: iRobot è così sicura dei suoi Roomba da farteli provare a casa per 30 giorni
items.summary: Il Roomba si porta a casa, si mette al lavoro sui propri pavimenti e, se non convince, si restituisce entro 30 giorni con il rimborso del prezzo pagato. Vale anche sui modelli in offerta ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Un robot aspirapolvere si sceglie leggendo le schede, ma si giudica solo a casa propria, tra il divano e il tappeto del soggiorno. Per questo iRobot ha deciso di togliere di mezzo il dubbio. Chi compra un Roomba ha 30 giorni per provarlo nella vita di tutti i giorni e, se non lo convince, lo restituisce e riceve indietro i soldi. Il programma si chiama Soddisfatti o Rimborsati e sarà attivo fino al 31 marzo 2027 .

Dietro c'è un ragionamento semplice. Un'azienda propone una prova così lunga solo quando è convinta che, dopo un mese di pulizie, il robot si sarà guadagnato il suo posto in casa.

Passerà sotto il letto? E sul tappeto a pelo lungo si arrampicherà o rimarrà impigliato? Riuscirà a stare dietro al pelo del gatto che cambia stagione? Come laverà il mio parquet? Sono le domande che si fa chiunque stia per comprare un robot , e nessuna scheda tecnica può rispondere per una casa che non conosce.

Trenta giorni bastano per scoprirlo . In pochissimo tempo un Roomba impara la pianta dell'appartamento e si abitua a soglie e bordi dei tappeti, passando dal parquet del soggiorno alle piastrelle del bagno. Chi ha animali lo vede al lavoro nei giorni normali, quelli in cui il pelo si accumula negli angoli e sotto i mobili. E chi vuole avere sempre un pavimento lavato di fresco potrà testare anche le capacità di lavare e asciugare il rullo del robot sulla base AutoWash dei modelli che la prevedono, per evitare muffe e cattivi odori.

È anche il modo migliore per apprezzare i Roomba più recenti . Il 115 e i Plus 415, 515 e 575 hanno un profilo fino al 21% più sottile del Roomba Plus 505. Se sulla carta è un numero, sotto il proprio divano diventa la polvere che finalmente sparisce.

Il meccanismo è pensato per non complicare la vita a chi compra.

1. Si acquista il Roomba da un qualunque rivenditore, in negozio oppure online.

2. Entro 10 giorni dall'acquisto lo si registra su irobot.it , caricando lo scontrino o la conferma d'ordine.

3. Si usa il robot in casa , come si farebbe con qualunque elettrodomestico appena comprato.

4. Se non convince, entro 30 giorni dall'acquisto si chiede il reso dalla propria area riservata . Un corriere passa a ritirarlo senza costi e il prezzo pagato torna con un bonifico.

L'unica accortezza è conservare la scatola originale e lo scontrino , perché il Roomba torna indietro completo, come è arrivato.

La prova vale anche quando il Roomba si compra in promozione. Chi approfitta di uno sconto da un rivenditore conserva i suoi 30 giorni e, in caso di reso, riceve indietro quanto ha effettivamente pagato. Restano fuori soltanto i Roomba ottenuti come omaggio, per esempio in un'offerta 3x2, o vinti come premio di un concorso.

Con le offerte di ottobre ancora in corso , è il momento più conveniente per mettere un Roomba alla prova .

Sul negozio ufficiale di iRobot i 30 giorni ci sono già "di serie", per ogni acquisto . Chi ordina da irobot.it non deve registrarsi al programma. Se il robot non lo convince, lo restituisce con la normale procedura di reso del sito, entro 30 giorni dalla consegna.

Il programma non si limita a qualche modello di punta. Comprende i Roomba d'ingresso come il 115 , i Plus delle serie 400, 500 e 600, i Max delle serie 700 e 800, fino al Mini Combo. Valgono anche le versioni proposte su Amazon. L'unica condizione è che il robot sia nuovo e distribuito in Italia da Nital, con il Sigillo di Garanzia Ufficiale Italia sulla confezione.

Se ci si vuole affidare a punti vendita fisici, il rivenditore più vicino si trova con la ricerca dei rivenditori di iRobot , mentre la pagina del programma spiega come registrarsi . Per l'elenco completo dei modelli e tutte le condizioni del rimborso conviene leggere il regolamento .

items.title: America has lost 200k of jobs in media, film and the arts. How much is AI?
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.apricitas.io/p/ai-and-the-fall-of-the-creative-class Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50226419 Points: 410 # Comments: 441
items.content:
Thanks for reading! If you haven’t subscribed, please click the button below:

By subscribing, you’ll join over 80,000 people who read Apricitas!

America has lost more than 200k jobs in “creative” industries over the last four years, with roughly 50k lost within the last year alone. That makes for one of the worst stretches for media employment in modern US history, with similar job loss intensity and duration occurring only during the major economic recessions of 2001 and 2008. Yet there’s no generalized recession today—instead, this period of job loss coincides with the rise of AI systems that can compose wholesale novels, photorealistic images, soundalike music, and practically every other form of digital art, en masse and at extremely low costs. Is this the fall of the Creative Class?

Proving the exact amount of AI-driven job loss in the arts is extremely difficult. Media firms are decidedly coy about their AI use, both to protect against public backlash and, more financially important, to preserve the legal basis for their copyrights. The effects of AI are also hard to disentangle from other factors currently affecting arts businesses, like consolidation in Hollywood, offshoring of content production, or the continued displacement of traditional media providers in favor of social media creators. Yet perhaps the clearest evidence of AI’s influence is just that all subsectors of the digital arts industry are losing jobs, while in-person entertainment is still growing at a healthy pace.

Some of those digital job losses are just a continuation of prior trends, like in the publishing industry where technological change has been continually grinding away newspaper and magazine jobs for decades. Yet for sectors like live broadcasting, streaming, or graphic design, recent experience is an unusual downturn compared to the tranquility of years prior. Then there’s the worst-hit sector, movie & sound recording, which has been bleeding jobs at a nearly unprecedented pace over the last three years.

Hollywood has never seen a stretch as bad as the last four years, with the movie & TV industry losing more than 100k jobs, nearly one-third of the sector’s total. At the depths touched this summer, total employment was lower than at any point since the 2008 recession and approaching the lowest point in 30 years. The streaming era has proven an extremely difficult transition, with traditional films and TV shows losing watch time to user-generated and increasingly AI-assisted or AI-generated content flows.

Overall, nearly half the media job losses of the last four years have been concentrated in the movie & sound recording sector that includes Hollywood. Written publishing has been the next-largest source of job loss, with employment down by more than 70k over the same time frame. Yet the job losses have by no means been contained to any particular part of media; instead they’ve hit nearly every subsector at some point. Nor do they show any sign of abating, with losses consistently hovering at around 50k per year and even accelerating in recent months. Will further AI development continue displacing workers in creative industries?

To understand what could happen to the business of art amidst the rise of AI, it’s important to understand what did happen to it during the first digital transition, the rise of the internet.

It was the turn of the millennium, and Metallica had a problem. Demos of their upcoming, unreleased tracks were bouncing around radio and the internet, originally leaked onto a new internet file-sharing website called Napster. There they found thousands of files shared amongst hundreds of thousands of users, many of which were direct rips of albums that sold for $15 being offered for free. The most anticipated albums were often leaked online even before they were on store shelves. Metallica sued Napster for copyright infringement, and they were soon joined by separate suits from other prominent artists and eventually the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA).

Much of the general public was understandably unsympathetic to Metallica , perceived as a bunch of already-successful millionaires trying to bilk even more money from listeners, and were even less sympathetic towards the RIAA, perceived as scurrilous middlemen who take from artists and fans alike. But the two of them easily won their lawsuit, forcing Napster into bankruptcy. Yet Metallica may have been right on the law but were on the wrong side of technology; the RIAA had won the battle but was losing the war.

The modern internet made file-sharing extremely easy, and no matter how much whac-a-mole companies played, they could not possibly catch every illegal upload. The perennial threat of piracy undermined their copyright and limited their ability to charge for music. Eventually, the value of individual songs fell to the point that companies like Spotify and Apple Music could swoop in to acquire massive catalogues, consolidate them, and charge a comparatively trivial fee for access. For what a single Metallica album would have cost in 2000, you can now get a month’s worth of unlimited access to nearly all human-made music.

The music industry has never returned to the heyday paydays of the peak CD era—even without adjusting for inflation, streaming revenue pales in comparison to ‘90s physical media sales. This was a massive boon to consumers, but it was also a squeeze on musicians that forced them to fundamentally change their business model over time. Instead of just selling records to earn money directly, music itself increasingly became a loss-leading advertisement for the live concerts (and merch) that provided a growing share of artists’ income. Tours got longer, venues got bigger, ticket prices skyrocketed, and musicians frequently took on roles closer to public influencers than isolated artistes. Were it not for rising concert sales, the business model of music would have completely collapsed, and the income going to musicians would have cratered.

Of course, there were still significant downsides to the transition into the streaming era. Bands (especially smaller ones) complain about the unending pressure to always be on tour. Musicians whose content was suited to home listening lost out to those more suited to giant festivals. Even accounting for concert revenues, musicians made less money than before. Yet musicians fared better than many areas of entertainment subsectors because there was a live component to fall back on—for many media industries, the digital era left no such comfort.

Over time, the business of video has moved in the opposite direction of music—out of the theatre and into the home. Hollywood formerly made most of its money enticing customers to visit sold-out movie theatres, but these were gradually supplanted by broadcast TV, cable, and physical media. Yet because each successful technological leap increased total video watch time, the industry was still able to thrive amidst technological upheaval. That is, until the modern streaming era.

Today, the plethora of video options and the rise of social media have sent video producers into a vicious competition for limited attention. Even before adjusting for inflation, movie ticket sales ended last year down 25% from their 2019 peak, cable revenue is down 18% from its peak, and streaming revenue has not been able to compensate for the drop. The mountain of free user-generated content on YouTube, Twitch, TikTok, or social media was already presenting harsh competition for traditional video companies in the years before ChatGPT’s launch, and now streaming services are also competing with a flood of AI-generated content. The business model of video media is fundamentally getting squeezed, and unlike in the music industry, there’s basically no equivalent to live concerts that Hollywood can be used to ease the pain.

The actual worst-case scenario for creative workers amidst the AI revolution is something similar to what happened to the publishing industry after the advent of the internet—that is, near-total collapse of their fundamental business model. Newspapers used to employ roughly half a million people in the US, more than the entire oil industry, and now their payrolls are down nearly 85% and still dropping. Magazine publishers likewise have let 66% of their staff go since the 90s, while book publishers have lost 40%.

The routine informational updates that previously formed newspapers’ bread-and-butter were all de-bundled—box scores moved to sports websites, stock movements went to financial websites, forecasts went to weather websites—each loss compounding on itself to undermine consumers’ need to buy the paper. Search engines became the first place people looked to for information, and newspapers’ advertising revenue rapidly started flowing to companies like Google instead. The collective of social media users became faster at breaking any news story than a daily paper could ever hope to be. When papers eventually did start aggressively paywalling content, the internet made it trivially easy for people to just copy the articles’ content and share it beyond the paywall. The entire business model had collapsed, to the point that now only a select few major newspapers can even survive.

items.title: The bitter row over military service that could shape Israel's future
items.summary: The ultra-Orthodox community is resisting being drafted into the Israeli army. But will they now bring down the Netanyahu government?
items.content:
Furious protesters are denouncing Israeli security forces as "Nazis" - but this is not a scene from a pro-Palestinian rally on the streets of London or Paris. This clash is in the heart of Israel, in which hundreds of ultra-Orthodox men in white shirts, black fedoras and long black frock coats face off against the military police.

The flashpoint is a building in the city of Modi'in, midway between Jerusalem and Tel Aviv, where a young ultra-Orthodox Jewish (or Haredi) man lives. The police have come to arrest him after he failed to report for military service.

The clash in early October, seen by the BBC in a video, is one of many in recent months in which one of the deepest schisms in Israeli society has become ever more exposed.

This widening fault line is playing out against the backdrop of the wars Israel is currently fighting, including the unresolved conflict against Hamas in Gaza - as well as increasing violence by extremist settlers against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.

Once a tiny minority, the ultra-Orthodox remain a group apart even as their numbers expand year by year. Currently, they are estimated to make up about 14% of the population, and the birth rate within the community remains far higher than among other Israelis. If their numbers continue to grow at a similar rate, they could make up one-third of the Jewish Israeli population by 2050.

As the ultra-Orthodox community becomes bigger, so has the debate around the expense of supporting them with stipends so they can devote themselves to full-time religious study. Subsidies to the group are estimated to cost the government 35bn shekels (£8.4bn) per year and, until recently, they were exempted from military service.

Now they're no longer an insignificant minority, they're facing pressure to engage more with wider Israeli society.

National security and the economy are two of the key issues this election. That means the division between the ultra-Orthodox and the majority of Israelis who believe they are not contributing their fair share to either is starker than ever.

With no outright majority likely for any current political alliance, and the future of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in doubt, the role of smaller parties - including Haredi parties - will once again be crucial in deciding who will govern Israel.

To have any chance of staying in power, Netanyahu needs to keep the ultra-Orthodox parties on side, however much pressure there is within Israel for their special status to be diminished.

From the ultra-Orthodox perspective, their social contract with the Israeli state is increasingly coming under pressure. Their all but exclusive focus on the study of Judaism's religious texts - such as the Torah, the Jewish Bible - means their education system is separate and many Haredim are not part of Israel's workforce.

For the ultra-Orthodox, the biggest issue of all is holding on to the exemption from serving in the IDF for students at traditional religious - or yeshiva - institutions. This dates back to the earliest days of the Israeli state when the Haredim were a miniscule community of survivors struggling to rebuild from the near extinction of the Holocaust.

But as Israel has become more embattled after the attacks of October 7, fighting wars on several fronts, their near complete absence from the country's conscription army has become more controversial.

Religious students and their rabbis believe that if young ultra-Orthodox men enter the military, they will be exposed to influences and behaviours that may decisively turn them away from their community. Beyond that, they believe that their staying true to the traditions of their community is vital for the very survival not only of Israel but the Jewish people.

When asked not long after October 7 why the ultra-Orthodox didn't contribute more to the military in such an emergency, one of the community's most senior leaders, Rabbi Dov Landau, said that not only should religious students not serve in the army, but they shouldn't even visit the wounded or attend the funerals of soldiers.

The rabbi said that in a time of such danger, only Torah students could protect Israel spiritually. "Salvation only comes through Torah learning, orderly Torah learning. And any neglect of or disruption to Torah learning, woe and alas for what will happen… The more Torah learners multiply, the more Torah learners increase their learning, the better. They protect us."

It would be a considerable understatement to say that this view is not shared by wider Israeli society. Polls have shown public support for conscripting the ultra-Orthodox surge throughout the war in Gaza. Many see it as a dereliction of responsibility by the Haredi community, made all the more galling by the fact that such a stance comes at the expense of taxpayers. The IDF has bemoaned a deficit in manpower, while many Israelis have had to serve hundreds of days in the past three years.

Dahlia Scheindlin is a leading political consultant and pollster in Israel. She says this issue is critical for Netanyahu and is key to understanding this moment in Israeli society against the backdrop of the war in Gaza, particularly among the political right. "Really the most burning, more immediate issue is the right-wing communities who are furious at the government for protecting the blanket exemption from the IDF at a time when, especially among the right, but really everybody in the Jewish community in Israel, is serving and many dying in these wars."

Two years ago, the Supreme Court ruled that the exemption for ultra-Orthodox men from serving in the military was effectively null and void. That could have meant that those dedicated to full-time religious study would now be drafted.

The reaction from the Haredi community was one of fury. Hundreds of thousands of Haredim held protests, blocking the main highways. And as with the incident in Modi'in, they tried to prevent the arrest of religious students for evading conscription. Protests have continued off and on, and densely-populated Haredi areas are often the backdrops for confrontation with the security forces.

There are two parties that have traditionally represented the Haredi community. One is United Torah Judaism – or UTJ – and represents Ashkenazi Jews, or Jews of European origin. The other is Shas, which was formed later and represents the Sephardi and Mizrahi – Jews from North Africa and the Middle East. They share a core agenda, which puts religious study above all else, including any questions around relations with the Palestinians.

Both UTJ and Shas have been part of Netanyahu's coalition - and they used their political clout to find ways to try to block enforcement of the Supreme Court ruling. On several occasions, they threatened to pull out of the alliance and bring the government down. UTJ acted on this but continued to support the government from outside, while Shas remained within the coalition.

Centre-right politician Gadi Eisenkot, who's shaped up as Netanyahu's main rival in this month's election, does not support their stance. He has made clear his belief that the idea of the ultra-Orthodox constituting a separate state within Israel with its own rules has become increasingly toxic. "A country that sends its best sons and daughters to fight and sacrifice their lives cannot tolerate a reality in which a state within a state exists," he said.

All this has meant that the issue of conscription exemption for ultra-Orthodox men is the number one priority on the electoral agenda of both Shas and UTJ.

A recent remark by a UTJ parliamentary candidate, Eliakim Stark, has raised the temperature further. He compared the plight of ultra-Orthodox men evading the military draft to the persecution of Jews during the Holocaust. It triggered furious rebukes from opposition leaders from across the political spectrum.

Daniel Goldman, an activist who specialises in Haredi issues, says that the two main Haredi parties feel increasingly embattled and less open to compromise.

He says the ultra-Orthodox don't believe that the state really needs their boys to bolster numbers. "It's at least partly down to the fact that the Haredi parties see the state as wanting to take their boys out of the community and change them from ultra-Orthodox to either regular religious or secular, God forbid, as they perceive it," he says. "And so in that environment of tension, they've actually hardened their positions."

Yitzhak Goldknopf from the UTJ, a former minister, has gone so far as to issue an ultimatum: "The Haredim will not change their way of life because there is an army and a war... If there is no choice and they must leave the country, they will leave."

But this is having a clear impact on the electoral fortunes of the Netanyahu coalition - of which Shas in particular has long been a key part. Without them, Netanyahu's alliance would fall short of the more than 60 seats needed for a majority in the Knesset.

Dahlia Scheindlin, the Israeli pollster, says that the refusal to give up the draft exemption by Shas and UTJ is damaging Netanyahu's coalition. "It is one of the main reasons why the coalition is unable to win back the kind of support that they had in 2022 when they won 64 seats," she says. "They're currently polling at about 50 to 52 seats."

items.title: Why the King's Caribbean tour could be 'biggest risk of his reign'
items.summary: The meticulously-planned visit takes in three countries in nine days - but is not without jeopardy.
items.content:
The planning is meticulous and dates back months, sometimes years, but there is always jeopardy.

King Charles III's visit to the Caribbean, which starts on Tuesday, takes him to three countries in nine days: the Bahamas, Guyana and finally Antigua and Barbuda for the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (Chogm).

It also throws him directly into the heat of the debate over the payment of reparations - compensation from countries that took part in the slave trade - alongside questions of whether the King should be apologising for the UK's role in what he has previously described as an "appalling atrocity" that leaves an "indelible stain" on history.

"This is the biggest risk of his reign so far with so much just outside of his control," said author and historian Sir Anthony Seldon. "Questions about slavery, reparations and apologies mean the moral integrity of the monarchy is being questioned."

The King will make three significant speeches during the Caribbean trip and will follow government advice not to issue an official apology for Britain's role in the transatlantic slave trade.

A senior royal aide said that the King would "not shy away from the darkest days of our past" but stressed that decisions over apologies and reparations were matters for government.

The current Burnham administration, like those before it, will not pay reparations.

Buckingham Palace says that acknowledging the wrongs of the past will be built into the King's programme in all three countries.

But apologies, reparations, and republicanism are rich pickings for campaigners and protests are likely.

This is the reality for the King and Buckingham Palace, and they are accepting of it.

Those who've worked on the planning of the trip view protests as part of the open debate in the region and security preparations include their possibility.

Lurking in the back of Royal Household minds will also be memories of the last tour by senior royals to the Caribbean in the early part of 2022.

Then, as the Duke and Duchess of Cambridge, William and Catherine found themselves facing criticism over the optics of the trip - images of the royal couple reaching out to touch the outstretched hands of Jamaican children through a wire fence looked clumsy. Engagements designed as tributes to past royal visits appeared outdated. And protests also caused the cancellation of a small part of the schedule.

Everything will have been done to avoid those kinds of missteps on the 2026 Caribbean tour.

The leadership in the Bahamas, Guyana and Antigua and Barbuda will celebrate the King and his work in protecting rainforests, creating cultural ties and reinforcing relationships around trade, energy, and agriculture.

The leaders of all three countries have voiced their support for reparatory justice.

In Antigua and Barbuda and the Bahamas, where the King is head of state, the conversation about becoming a republic has significant support.

Elected officials in the former no longer have to pledge allegiance to the King ending a 40-year tradition of swearing loyalty to the monarch.

"He pulled off an extraordinary triumph with President Trump in his US visit earlier this year and stood up to him and put him in his place in a way that no leader has done - while not incurring his wrath," said Sir Anthony. "If he can deal with the delicate nature of this trip for him personally, for the British monarchy, and the future of the Commonwealth, it could be an enormous success."

This Caribbean tour has to cut through a sea of royal distractions.

The King has spent much of the past three months in Scotland, where he is based over the summer.

It should have been a quieter time in the royal calendar, but it has been quite the opposite.

The surprise return of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex to the UK has been noisy. The level of coverage Harry and Meghan get is unsettling and, at times, irritating for the Royal Family.

The King's youngest son has not yet seen his father in person, but they are said to have talked.

Then enter Earl Spencer, the King's former brother-in-law, with his memoir, Swan Song, criticising the King's response to the death of Diana, Princess of Wales. It triggered a strong pushback from the Palace.

And in recent days, the serious claims made about Meghan's father, Thomas Markle, have drawn his daughter into a complex tale involving global police forces, sexual abuse allegations and further family trauma.

An impactful and successful Caribbean tour is a chance to switch focus.

But if royal stories back home are running hot, it can be hard to focus minds on the King's engagements over four thousand miles (6,437km) away.

Former Foreign Secretary David Lammy, who has strong family ties to the Caribbean, has accompanied the King on a number of trips outside the UK.

"He is our head of state. He is amongst some of the most recognisable figures in the world. For a small country like Guyana, the validation of a state visit is huge," said the Tottenham MP whose father came to the UK from what was then British Guiana and who also has relatives in Antigua and Barbuda. "My mother would forever recall the Queen's visit in 1996."

But there was also a recognition of that royal trip jeopardy.

"Knowing Guyana, Antigua and Barbuda as well as I do, he will be overwhelmingly received positively," Lammy said. "But these are lively democracies in which of course there will be some dissent."

A transatlantic flight, three countries over nine days and about 36 separate engagements when you're closing in on your 78th birthday is an intense schedule. It is also a reminder that the King is still dealing with a cancer diagnosis and having regular treatment. Buckingham Palace has reiterated its position that he is on a "positive trajectory".

Queen Camilla will only accompany the King on the Antigua and Barbuda leg of the visit for Chogm and a number of other engagements, including some around her own areas of interest – literacy and supporting efforts to end violence against women and girls.

The Queen, who will be 80 next July, is known to find the pace and hot conditions of some royal tours gruelling.

This is a trip that comes with potential pitfalls but also the possibility of great reward for the King.

"The King can be an extraordinarily empathetic and in tune figure," Sir Anthony said.

items.title: From Russian cages to Irish sanctuary: The five-year rescue journey of Bu and Tyapa
items.summary: For Bu and Tyapa, the five-year journey from Russia to the Irish countryside was anything but straightforward.
items.content:
After years in cramped cages, two brown bears are adjusting to their new life following a remarkable rescue mission that spanned multiple countries, was disrupted by two major conflicts and involved more than 100 people.

For Bu and Tyapa, the five-year rescue journey from the Republic of Dagestan in Russia to the Irish countryside was anything but straightforward.

One bear had spent their life forced to perform in a circus, while the other was confined to a cage so small they could not stand upright.

Today, the bears are now adjusting to a totally different world among the trees and grass at Wild Ireland, a sanctuary for rescued animals in County Donegal.

Wild Ireland founder Killian McLaughlin first learned about Bu and Tyapa in 2021 and committed to bringing them to safety in Donegal.

The sanctuary, located in Burnfoot, opened in October 2019 and provides a safe space for animals, including brown bears, monkeys, wolves, and lynx.

McLaughlin said the two bears were in extremely poor health when they were first rescued.

Former circus bear Bu had spent years confined to a small indoor cage after being forced to perform.

McLaughlin said Tyapa had lived in a cage measuring just 2.5m by 2.5m by 2m, which was too low for him to stand upright and had no roof, which left him exposed to the harsh winters and blistering summer heat.

The bear had no water dish and relied on a hose for drinking water. McLaughlin said he was being raised to be killed for an eventual taxidermy display.

When the bears were rescued, both were severely malnourished and showed signs of psychological trauma.

Blood tests also revealed serious kidney problems associated with prolonged dehydration.

Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 made the original transport route through Ukraine impossible, said McLaughlin.

An alternative route through the Middle East was then explored, but plans were disrupted again in February 2026 when the escalating conflict involving Iran led to airspace closures and flight disruptions across the region.

More than 100 people were involved in the rescue operation, including volunteers, lawyers, veterinarians, animal transport specialists, cargo teams and officials in Russia, the United Arab Emirates and Ireland.

In late October 2025, Dima and Yana Kim, who work at Tiger House, a sanctuary near St Petersburg that cares for former circus tigers, embarked on a 36-hour drive to Dagestan to rescue the bears.

Bu and Tyapa had to be cut out of their rusting steel cages, sedated and placed in secure transport crates for the journey back to Tiger House, where they received veterinary treatment and underwent quarantine.

After months of preparation and repeated delays, the bears eventually travelled from Moscow via Abu Dhabi to Dublin, arriving in Ireland in August.

Since arriving at Wild Ireland, McLaughlin said both bears have gained weight, their coats have improved, and follow-up blood tests have shown that their kidney function has returned to normal.

He said their habitat provides woodland, water and room to explore, as well as sheltered areas where they can retreat or move out of public view if they would like some privacy.

"These bears have suffered trauma and the first step of that recovery process is get them back out into the forest, get their paws into the soil and on the grass and get them exploring.

Working with bears is certainly not your everyday job, but for Wild Ireland team member Chloe McElhatton, it's one she absolutely relishes.

Chloe has been working at Wild Ireland for just over a year. She studied zoology at Queen's University Belfast, completing a four-year degree before joining the team.

"This is obviously a very unique job, and it's quite different from what most people would do," she said.

"We've done a lot of work hiding food around the bear habitats, encouraging them to search and forage for it themselves and this promotes their natural behaviours and helps them become more comfortable in that new open space," she said.

"Over time, we've seen their confidence build, and you can see great changes, both physically and mentally, in both of them."

Liam, who is from France, said the bears were one of his favourite animals to see when visiting the park.

"Very big and very impressive," is how he summed up Bu and Tyapa.

"I saw chickens, some wolves and some monkeys and then the bears which were definitely my favourite."

Chris Roberts is from Manorcunningham, about 20 minutes from Wild Ireland, and has been visiting the site ever since it first opened in 2019.

"I've lost count of how many times we've been here, but we really wanted to come down today to see if we could catch a glimpse of Bu and Tyapa.

"We absolutely loved it and are delighted to see them doing so well, especially considering their backstory and the awful conditions they were once kept in."

items.title: A shark went astray and captured Korea's heart - will she finally make it back to sea?
items.summary: More than a million people flocked to Busan to catch a glimpse of the female dusky shark they called Bukangi.
items.content:
As soon as a large shark was spotted in a canal in Busan - a bustling shipping hub and beach city on South Korea's south-eastern tip - marine biologist Kim Hyun-woo was drafted in to rescue it.

He got the call in mid-September, on his way home from a business trip tracking shoals of mackerel to aid fishing vessels. Despite being one of the country's leading shark experts, he never thought he'd be asked by the coastguard to actually save one.

South Korea is no stranger to sharks but one this size, in a shallow, concrete canal right by the world's seventh busiest port, was unheard of - until now.

With an excited crowd already gathering at the waterfront, his team from the National Institute of Fisheries Science had to move fast.

Some sharks are more dangerous than others. The star of the 1975 blockbuster Jaws, the great white shark, is known to attack and kill humans.

The specimen in Busan was found to be a female dusky shark, a species linked only to two deadly attacks. Still, Kim feared someone in the crowd might jump or fall into the canal.

A small coastguard ship made an initial attempt using an electrical deterrence device, which generates a weak current that sharks avoid.

They're usually used after sightings near popular beaches. But after five hours, officials determined this particular shark was too large and fast for the device.

Kim changed tack, deciding instead to wait for the shark to let herself out. But that did not happen.

As authorities looked for ways to guide her out of the canal, the stranded creature went viral.

Just hours after she appeared, the council had sent everyone in the city an emergency text alert, urging pedestrians and residents to "exercise caution for their safety".

People rarely visited the park along the canal but because of the message, the place was soon brimming with people eager to spot the shark.

Adoring fans named her Bukangi, from "buk hang", the Korean name of the nearby harbour. Within days, a business trademarked it and Bukangi pins, plushies and T-shirts began selling online.

City authorities joined in, livestreaming the shark and making her their official mascot.

A banner was hung at the entrance of the canal, asking the public to sign a petition "on behalf of Bukangi" to demand the national government's support for the construction of a new 30,000-seater baseball stadium by the canal.

Shark spotting became a team effort among locals and visitors. The unspoken rule was that children were given the front row, and whoever saw Bukangi had to point her out to newer arrivals.

Some self-appointed defenders even patrolled the canal at night to make sure no-one was shining torches or lasers at Bukangi.

More than 1.6 million visitors ultimately flocked to the canal.

The local mayor said the shark brought "the kind of publicity even billions of dollars cannot buy" to the port.

"It's really rare these days for people to come together," said Kim Joo-eun, who came to see the shark with her two nieces. "I feel that Bukangi brought us all together, cheering for her… It's a lot of fun."

As September drew to an end, she hadn't been seen feeding for days and was spotted with bloody abrasions on her snout from bumping into the concrete walls.

Prominent marine biology professor Choi Yoon told local media that experts were particularly worried about a "critical" injury around the shark's eye.

At the end of September, Kim's team mounted another rescue attempt. The marine biologist looked back to a 2004 incident in Massachusetts, when water jets were used to drive a great white shark away from a shallow pond.

But when the team tried this on Bukangi, she kept circling back.

On 2 October, they decided to install a net spanning the width of the canal to stop her from returning. She managed to swim around the net and was back within hours.

At this point, Kim started thinking the shark might have problems with her snout's electromagnetic sensors, which she uses for navigation. Or she might have become confused by the loud noises emitted by ships in the harbour.

The reason Bukangi was even in the canal may be a sign of warming seas, the oceans ministry suggests.

It believes she may have followed plentiful fish to warmer waters. Some 50 large sharks were recorded off South Korea's east coast in the first half of the year; four times as many as last year.

With each failed attempt some of Bukangi's newfound fans began demanding she be left in peace.

On Thursday, several showed up with placards and shouted "leave Bukangi alone" and "remove the net".

When a security guard told them to stop, one man cried: "I love you, Bukangi!"

"I am obsessed with her," said Jeong Yo-won, a woman in her 40s. She called the shark a "source of hope and joy" and insisted, "I don't think we should evict her mercilessly like this."

"I would stare at her for hours because I was so enamoured by her," a woman said after sighting the shark on her third attempt. "I hope Bukangi would stay, but I prefer that she lives a long and healthy life."

People joked the council should "make an official ID for Bukangi and give a pension", Shin Seungmin said.

"She brought so much fun with her. But she should go and live her normal shark life."

Staying in the canal would seriously jeopardise Bukangi because of falling autumn temperatures, Kim explains. Usually this prompts sharks to migrate to warmer waters further south.

"This canal is far from something we can call a habitat," he adds. "A wild animal cannot stay in a space made strictly for humans."

Eventually, as public scrutiny grew, the oceans ministry took over the rescue operation from the fisheries institute. Around 40 personnel, including divers from Busan's aquarium, were mobilised. A vet was on standby, along with an ambulance in case the divers were attacked by Bukangi.

On Wednesday divers installed two layers of nets, and Bukangi was successfully herded out of the narrow canal into open water. But overnight, she swam back into the canal, diving under the outer net.

Then on thursday, rescuers removed the outer layer, and Bukangi was seen swimming further and further towards open sea.

Although she did occasionally circle back, the rescue operation had ended.

There have been no sightings of Bukangi in the last few days, which experts say is a positive sign.

Prof Choi believes she may be adjusting to wider, deeper waters.

She is unlikely to have travelled far, he adds, and could reappear over the coming week.

But he is also worried about any injuries she may have sustained. Trapped in the canal, it "kept scraping against [the walls], stripping the skin off its snout and even its pectoral fins", he told local media.

For now, South Korea is holding its breath, hoping Bukangi can find her way back to her home - the open sea.

Se gli iraniani dovessero dotarsi di armi nucleari, nient'altro avrebbe più importanza. Tutto il resto impallidisce di fronte al pericolo esistenziale rappresentato dall'Iran e dall'asse sciita. Raid sull’Università di Gaza fa tre morti, altre quattro vittime nella Striscia

Almeno tre sono le persone che hanno perso la vita a seguito di un raid aereo israeliano sull'Università di Gaza City, dove altre otto persone sono rimaste ferite. Lo riferiscono fonti mediche e dello staff dell'ateneo, mentre la protezione civile della Striscia di Gaza riferisce di altri quattro morti oggi nell'enclave. L'esercito israeliano ha detto che sta verificando. L'ospedale al Shifa ha dichiarato di aver ricevuto tre corpi e di aver curato otto persone rimaste ferite nell'attacco con droni a Gaza City, mentre due fonti dell'Università Islamica hanno affermato che le vittime erano membri del personale amministrativo e i feriti studenti. Il ministero dell'Istruzione di Gaza ha dichiarato in un comunicato che gli studenti sono rimasti feriti mentre erano in aula a seguire le lezioni. Il ministero nota inoltre che "il 95% degli istituti accademici di Gaza sono stati distrutti a causa della guerra". Il portavoce della protezione civile di Gaza, Mahmoud Bassal, ha inoltre spiegato che due persone sono state uccise in un raid aereo israeliano nella città meridionale di Khan Yunis, una nella zona centrale di Deir al Balah e una nel nord della Striscia di Gaza

Media: “Mediatori del Qatar a Teheran per prevenire l’escalation”

Una delegazione inviata dal Qatar è arrivata oggi a Teheran nell'ambito degli sforzi di mediazione volti a prevenire un'escalation delle tensioni nella regione. Lo ha riferito una fonte informata a 'The New Arab'. Il Jerusalem Post sottolinea che la missione diplomatica è in coordinamento con gli Stati Uniti

“Cripto contro sanzioni?” La Banca centrale critica Netanyahu

La Banca centrale israeliana ha espresso una rara condanna delle recenti dichiarazioni del primo ministro Benjamin Netanyahu, il quale ha suggerito che il Paese utilizzi le criptovalute per contribuire a creare un'"economia alternativa" in grado di resistere a possibili sanzioni. Le dichiarazioni avevano già suscitato critiche da parte degli avversari di Netanyahu nelle elezioni in programma martedì, i quali hanno affermato che equivalevano a un'ammissione tacita del fatto che la leadership del premier stesse generando conseguenze dannose per Israele. "Le criptovalute non possono essere utilizzate come mezzo per aggirare le sanzioni contro Israele. Ciò che è giusto per l'economia israeliana è preservare le nostre relazioni economiche con i nostri principali partner commerciali e concentrarci sulla prevenzione delle sanzioni e del loro impatto negativo sull'economia", ha dichiarato la Banca d'Israele in un comunicato stampa ieri sera. In una recente intervista al Canale 10 israeliano, Netanyahu ha riconosciuto le crescenti pressioni da parte del suo principale alleato, gli Stati Uniti, e ha affermato che "potrebbero esserci sanzioni, comprese quelle bancarie". "E' necessario preparare un'economia alternativa che possa funzionare anche in assenza di sanzioni", ha aggiunto, dichiarando di aver ordinato la stesura di piani che utilizzino la tecnologia blockchain a tale scopo

Il primo ministro israeliano Benjamin Netanyahu ha avvertito che, qualora non venisse rieletto martedì, il Paese sarebbe a rischio di "un secondo Olocausto", a causa della persistente "minaccia esistenziale" rappresentata dall'Iran e dai suoi alleati regionali. "Abbiamo ancora due anni di amministrazione (Donald) Trump per completare il lavoro in Iran, e non è dato sapere cosa accadrà in seguito: se ci sarà Kamala Harris o qualcun altro", ha scritto Netanyahu sul suo profilo X, riportando le parole dello scrittore israeliano Yuval Bloomberg, accompagnate da un'immagine generata dall'intelligenza artificiale che ritrae un'esplosione nucleare su Tel Aviv. Il testo di Bloomberg, che il premier israeliano sposa completamente, sostiene che alcune delle questioni centrali di queste elezioni come il servizio militare obbligatorio per gli ultra-ortodossi, il ruolo del Qatar o l'eventuale ricezione, da parte dello stesso Netanyahu, di avvertimenti su un possibile attacco prima del 7 ottobre non siano "altro che un enorme fumogeno, volto a oscurare l'unica questione che sovrasta tutte le altre"

Eisenkot: “Netanyahu isterico, usa tattiche elettorali di menzogne e allarmismo”

"Netanyahu, sei in uno stato di isteria. Come in ogni campagna elettorale, stai ricorrendo ancora una volta alle solite tattiche: menzogne e allarmismo. Questa volta, minacci i cittadini di Israele prospettando un annientamento di massa, e tutto ciò dopo aver fallito nel raggiungere i tuoi obiettivi bellici nei confronti dell'Iran". Lo scrive su X Gadi Eisenkot, il principale rivale di Netanyahu nella campagna elettorale. "Hai fallito. E tra due giorni, il popolo di Israele te lo dimostrerà chiaramente alle urne. Formeremo il prossimo governo e guideremo Israele verso la sicurezza e la prosperità", ha aggiunto

Due morti in un raid di Israele su Gaza, tra cui bambina di 8 anni

Almeno due palestinesi sono stati uccisi da attacchi israeliani a Gaza, e molti altri sono rimasti feriti. Lo riporta Al Jazeera. Nello specifico, una bambina di otto anni è stata uccisa da colpi d'arma da fuoco israeliani nel centro di Deir el-Balah, mentre un altro palestinese è stato ucciso in un attacco dell'esercito ad al-Mazraa, a est di Deir el-Balah. Un attacco di droni israeliani contro un raduno nel campus dell'Università Islamica, a ovest di Gaza City, ha inoltre ferito diversi palestinesi, alcuni in modo grave. Il Ministero dell'Istruzione di Gaza ha dichiarato che 10 studenti e un insegnante sono stati uccisi negli attacchi israeliani nella Striscia tra il 18 e il 24 ottobre

Golan: “Netanyahu va tenuto lontano dai social, disconnesso dalla realtà”

“Il primo ministro di Israele ha pubblicato un'immagine di una bomba atomica sopra Tel Aviv. Bisogna tenerlo lontano dai social media. Lui e la sua cerchia ristretta hanno perso completamente il contatto con la realtà. La pressione sta aumentando. Martedì sostituiremo questi seminatori di paura e riporteremo sicurezza e buon senso in Israele". Lo scrive su X Yair Golan, leader del partito di sinistra I Democratici, in riferimento al post di Netanyahu in cui ha pubblicato un'immagine di una bomba atomica su Tel Aviv

Netanyahu posta foto di atomica su Tel Aviv: “Due anni per finire il lavoro con l'Iran”

Il primo ministro Benjamin Netanyahu ha pubblicato sul suo account X un'immagine che ritrae una bomba atomica che si abbatte su Tel Aviv, e condivide un post dello scrittore Yuval Blumberg, secondo cui "lo Stato di Israele deve affrontare una minaccia esistenziale reale e concreta. Se gli iraniani dovessero dotarsi di armi nucleari, nient'altro avrebbe più importanza. Tutto il resto impallidisce di fronte al pericolo esistenziale rappresentato dall'Iran e dall'asse sciita. Abbiamo ancora due anni di presidenza Trump per portare a termine il lavoro con l'Iran; dopodiché, è impossibile prevedere cosa accadrà: se subentrerà Kamala Harris o una figura analoga a Mamdani. Questo è l'arco di tempo che ci rimane. Tutte le risorse di cui lo Stato dispone devono essere investite in questa missione", si legge nel post. "Il Qatar, gli ultraortodossi, Urich, è tutto una cortina fumogena creata per oscurare l'unica questione che supera tutte le altre: se due bombe atomiche dovessero abbattesti sul centro di Israele, a chi importerebbe ancora di queste sterili polemiche?", aggiunge, con riferimento allo scandalo Qatargate che vede coinvolti alcuni collaboratori di Netanyahu, come Jonathan Urich

תקראו את הדברים החשובים של יובל בלומברג: מדינת ישראל נמצאת בסכנה קיומית אמיתית ומוחשית. אם האיראנים ישיגו גרעין, שום דבר כבר לא ישנה יותר. הכל כל כך טפל אל מול הסכנה הקיומית של איראן והציר השיעי. הסערות המבוימות והמומצאות חדשות לבקרים נועדו להסיט את תשומת הלב מהדבר האחד שהוא החשוב ביותר: סיום העבודה באיראן. זה נוגע בקיום הפיזי של כל אדם ואדם כאן. יש לנו עוד שנתיים של טראמפ לסיים את העבודה באיראן, ואין לדעת מה יהיה לאחר מכן, אם זו תהיה קמאלה האריס, או תואם מאמדני כלשהו. זה חלון הזמן שנותר לנו כדי להשלים את העבודה הנדרשת כדי להבטיח את הקיום הפיזי שלנו לשנים הבאות. כל משאבי המדינה הנדרשים, צריכים להיות מושקעים במשימה הזו. קטאר, חרדים, אוריך, גיוס, התראות. הכל מסך עשן ענקי כדי להסתיר את הנושא היחיד שניצב מעל כולם בפער. אם יפלו במרכז הארץ שתי פצצות אטום, את מי יעניינו כל סערות הסרק האלה? הדורות הבאים לא יסלחו לנו אם נפספס את חלון ההזדמנויות ההיסטורי שמאפשר לנו לנסות ולהשלים את המשימה הקריטית ביותר שעומדת בפני הדור שלנו. זה לא יקרה עם ראש ממשלה שמוחזק בצווארו על ידי האחים המוסלמים וסייעני הטרור. זה לא יקרה עם ראש ממשלה שלא מסוגל להרים את הטלפון ולנהל שיחה אינטימית רציפה עם טראמפ. זה לא יקרה עם ראש ממשלה שלא מסוגל לעמוד בלחץ של ראיון טלויזיה. השינאה לנתניהו, ככל שהיא עולם ומלואו עבור מחנה שלם, לא תעזור מול הגרעין האיראני. כל אחד שדואג לקיום הפיזי שלו, של משפחתו, ושל אהוביו, ידו צריכה לרעוד לפני שהוא בוחר במישהו שלא יהיה מסוגל להשלים את המשימה, ובכך לדון את עצמו ואת משפחתו לסכנה של שואה שניה, בגלל השינאה הפוליטית שלו או בגלל סערת דמה מטופשת וחסרת חשיבות.

items.title: Inarrestabile Kimi si prende la pole ad Austin: 'Voglio vincere'
items.summary: In Texas precede Verstappen. Primo match-point per il mondiale. Le Ferrari deludono
items.content:
Inarrestabile Kimi Antonelli che conquista la pole position nel Gp di Austin e si lancia all'inseguimento del titolo mondiale di Formula 1. In Texas l'attenzione è tutta per il giovane pilota della Mercedes che, complice una serie di difficili combinazioni nei piazzamenti, nella notte italiana di domenica potrebbe già laurearsi campione del mondo. Se così sarà non dipende solo dal 20enne di Bologna, ma da cosa faranno i suoi avversari in pista. Intanto, però, Antonelli svolge alla perfezione il proprio compito: miglior tempo nelle qualifiche e primo posto in griglia alla partenza.

Alle sue spalle Max Verstappen che, con la Red Bull, promette battaglia in gara. Più attardate le Ferrari con Charles Leclerc quarto e Lewis Hamilton quinto . Ancora più dietro la Mercedes di George Russell che si piazza settimo. Per tutto il weekend il 20enne bolognese ha marcato il territorio piazzandosi sempre tra i primi quattro in pista, consapevole, con il titolo ad un passo, di dover mantenere il sangue freddo senza rischiare troppo . Ma nelle qualifiche ha piazzato la zampata vincente. I rischi devono correrli soprattutto gli inseguitori se vogliono ancora puntare ad una improbabile rimonta. Alla vigilia della gara statunitense, Kimi ha 340 punti, con George Russell distaccato di 102 (238 punti) e Lewis Hamilton a -111 (229 punti). Al giovanissimo talento emiliano basterebbe, dopo la gara texana, avere 125 punti di vantaggio in classifica su Russell per avere la matematica certezza del titolo.

Calcoli che, però, sembrano non entusiasmare Antonelli: "Abbiamo fatto la pole e ora cercheremo di vincere. Ma Max è stato molto veloce e non sarà semplice. Cercherò di partire bene", ha spiegato subito dopo aver segnato il miglior tempo, lasciando intendere che non intende preoccuparsi di cosa faranno gli avversari anche perché tra una settimana si correrà in Messico e lì, finalmente, il titolo potrebbe diventare realtà. Il mondiale non è una ossessione per il giovanissimo talento Mercedes. I calcoli per il titolo sono difficili da fare anche perché non è ancora certo quante gare si disputeranno da qui alla fine della stagione.

Guerre permettendo, si dovrebbe correre regolarmente in Qatar e ad Abu Dhabi. Ma, se le due tappe in Medioriente dovessero essere cancellate e venisse confermato un unico recupero ad Imola, ad Antonelli basterebbe stare davanti a Russell o non perdere più di due punti in Texas . Tutte operazioni aritmetiche che però, al momento, non è possibile fare. Kimi, d'altronde, vuole vincere in pista tagliando per primo il traguardo, il resto lo lascia agli appassionati di numeri e statistica. In Italia, invece, si fanno i conti e bene con il pallottoliere: è da 73 anni che un italiano non vince il Mondiale di F1. L'ultimo fu Alberto Ascari.

items.title: Guerra Ucraina - Russia, news. Putin: “Accusarci per i disordini è incapacità dei leader europei”
items.summary: Mosca: “Pronti a riprendere i negoziati con Kiev dopo il 4 novembre”. Zelensky: “Quattro morti e 22 feriti in attacchi nella regione di Dnipro”. Attacco con droni russi a Kharkiv, raid ucraino su Belgorod
items.content:
Mosca è pronta a riprendere i colloqui trilaterali per una soluzione in Ucraina dopo il 4 novembre, data in cui la Russia celebra la Giornata dell'Unità Nazionale. Lo dice Yuri Ushakov , consigliere del presidente russo Vladimir Putin.

"Quasi ogni giorno" gli "attacchi brutali" della Russia in Ucraina "provocano morti e feriti", come quelli, avvenuti ieri sera, in cui sono rimaste uccise quattro persone nella regione di Dnipro: lo afferma stamane su X il leader di Kiev, Volodymyr Zelensky. "Altre 22 persone sono rimaste ferite, tra cui una bambina di 11 anni", aggiunge il presidente ucraino

Zelensky: “Quattro morti e 22 feriti in attacchi nella regione di Dnipro”

Mosca: “Pronti a riprendere i negoziati con Kiev dopo il 4 novembre”

Putin: “Accusarci per i disordini è segno di debolezza e incapacità dei leader europei”

Kiev: un morto e 4 feriti a Kharkiv dopo un attacco con droni russi

Mosca: “Già iniziati i preparativi per il vertice a tre Putin-Xi-Trump”

I preparativi organizzativi per un vertice trilaterale tra i leader di Russia, Cina e Stati Uniti, Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping e Donald Trump, "sono già iniziati": lo ha dichiarato il consigliere del presidente russo Yuri Ushakov a Vesti, programma di notizie della Tv di stato, ripresa dalla Tass. "Ora posso affermare con certezza che Mosca, Pechino e Washington sono, in linea di principio, pronte all'incontro trilaterale. I preparativi sono già cominciati", ha dichiarato il rappresentante del Cremlino

Zelensky: “Quattro morti e 22 feriti in attacchi nella regione di Dnipro”

"Quasi ogni giorno" gli "attacchi brutali" della Russia in Ucraina "provocano morti e feriti", come quelli, avvenuti ieri sera, in cui sono rimaste uccise quattro persone nella regione di Dnipro: lo afferma stamane su X il leader di Kiev, Volodymyr Zelensky. "Altre 22 persone sono rimaste ferite, tra cui una bambina di 11 anni", aggiunge il presidente ucraino

Mosca: “Pronti a riprendere i negoziati con Kiev dopo il 4 novembre”

Mosca è pronta a riprendere i colloqui trilaterali per una soluzione in Ucraina dopo il 4 novembre, data in cui la Russia celebra la Giornata dell'Unità Nazionale. Lo dice Yuri Ushakov, consigliere del presidente russo Vladimir Putin. "La prossima scadenza è il 4 novembre, la nostra grande festività. Dopodichè, saremo pronti a riprendere i negoziati", ha dichiarato Ushakov all'agenzia di stampa Vesti. Ushakov aveva precedentemente annunciato che Abu Dhabi, capitale degli Emirati Arabi Uniti, è in fase di valutazione come possibile sede per consultazioni trilaterali

Putin: “Accusarci per i disordini è segno di debolezza e incapacità dei leader europei”

Le accuse secondo cui la Russia starebbe orchestrando i disordini e le proteste in Europa "dimostrano la debolezza dei politici europei e la loro incapacità di assumersi la responsabilità degli eventi attuali". Lo ha detto il presidente russo Vladimir Putin in una intervista all'agenzia di stampa Vesti. "Questo dimostra la debolezza e l'incapacità di alcuni leader dei paesi europei di assumersi la responsabilità di ciò che sta accadendo", ha detto Putin. "Non c'è nulla di inaspettato. Come sappiamo, la Russia è sempre stata accusata di ogni peccato mortale", ha aggiunto

Le forze russe hanno colpito con un drone un edificio residenziale di cinque piani a Vinnytsia, nell'Ucraina centro-occidentale. Sei persone sono rimaste ferite. Lo riporta Rbc-Ucraina, citando la responsabile dell'Ova di Vinnytsia, Natalya Zabolotna . L'impatto ha causato danni tra il secondo e il terzo piano, quattro appartamenti sono stati completamente distrutti e le auto parcheggiate nelle vicinanze hanno subito danni. Sei persone sono rimaste ferite, una è stata ricoverata in ospedale. "A seguito del massiccio attacco nella regione, si sono registrate anche la distruzione di infrastrutture critiche e civili e danni ad abitazioni private".

Nel corso della notte, la Russia ha attaccato l'Ucraina con 153 droni di tipo Shahed, S8000 Banderol/Dan-T, Gerbera e Parodiya. Lo riferiscono i militari di Kiev. Secondo i dati preliminari, le forze di difesa aerea hanno abbattuto o neutralizzato 119 droni nemici. In particolare, un attacco russo su Vinnytsia e la regione circostante ha causato danni e un blackout parziale.

Attacco ucraino con droni nella regione di Perm, cinque feriti

Un attacco con droni nella regione russa di Perm ha danneggiato un impianto industriale, provocando il ferimento di cinque lavoratori: lo ha dichiarato il governatore regionale Dmitry Makhonin . I servizi di emergenza sono intervenuti sul posto e i feriti hanno ricevuto le necessarie cure mediche, ha riferito il governatore tramite l'applicazione di messaggistica Max.

Un civile è stato ucciso mentre altre 10 persone sono rimaste ferite a seguito degli attacchi dei droni delle forze armate ucraine nella regione russa di Belgorod. Lo ha riferito il centro operativo regionale per le emergenze.

Secondo quanto riferito da funzionari locali e da filmati di testimoni oculari pubblicati sui social media, nella notte un enorme sciame di droni ucraini ha attaccato la regione russa di Belgorod. Lo riferisce Kyiv Independent. Stando al canale di monitoraggio Exilenova-Plus, l'obiettivo è stato il centro commerciale MegaGrinn, il più grande complesso di negozi e intrattenimento di Belgorod che ospita più di 200 negozi, oltre a un supermercato, un cinema e ristoranti. La struttura era chiusa e deserta durante l'attacco notturno, ma ci sarebbero comunque dei feriti.

"Vorremmo tornare a una situazione in cui Russia e Ucraina raggiungano un accordo, così da poter fare affari con entrambe" ha detto Donald Trump parlando con i giornalisti in Florida prima di partire per la Georgia. "Di certo faremo affari sia con l'Ucraina che con la Russia una volta terminata questa guerra".

Musk: “Kiev ha violato termini servizio di Starlink, lo ha usato per raid con droni”

"L'esercito ucraino ha violato i termini di servizio di Starlink e lo ha utilizzato per attacchi con droni per uccidere persone. Quella lacuna è stata colmata la settimana scorsa". Lo ha affermato su X il miliardario americano e proprietario di SpaceX, Elon Musk, commentando le restrizioni all'accesso a Starlink, aggiungendo che se Starlink venisse disattivato, "il fronte ucraino crollerebbe all'istante". Lo riportano i media ucraini. Oggi l'Ucraina ha dichiarato che il sistema satellitare Starlink e la sua versione militare Starshield sono pienamente operativi dopo oltre una settimana di restrizioni che hanno interrotto le operazioni militari e intensificato le tensioni con gli Stati Uniti.

Kiev: un morto e 4 feriti a Kharkiv dopo un attacco con droni russi

"Un attacco di droni russi questa sera nel distretto di Novobavarskyi a Kharkiv ha causato un morto e quattro feriti". Lo ha annunciato il sindaco Igor Terekhov sui social media, scrive l'Ukrainska Pravda.

items.title: Who are the candidates in Brazil's presidential election?
items.summary: Voters in Sunday's election are choosing between two very different candidates, as Americas correspondent Ione Wells reports from Rio de Janeiro.
items.content:
Polls have opened in Brazil to vote for the country's next president.

Brazilians are choosing between Brazil's current left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and the right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

Bolsonaro, the son of imprisoned former president Jair Bolsonaro, beat Lula in the first round of voting on 4 October by a narrow margin.

Americas correspondent Ione Wells reports from Rio de Janeiro as voters choose between two very different candidates.

items.title: We should be more ambitious with the software we build
items.summary: Article URL: https://danluu.com/ambitious/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50225695 Points: 536 # Comments: 488
items.content:
Since early this year, Michael Malis (of pgrust ) has been showing me interesting things he's done and saying

There is, understandably, a lot of skepticism about projects like pgrust because there are so many low-quality AI-generated projects out there. If I didn't know Malis and didn't look into it, I would just assume that pgrust was another vibe slopped project that's never going to work. But I know Malis well enough to trust his work without looking into it, and if you look into it a bit, you'll see that in testing pgrust, he's testing thoroughly enough that he's even uncovering real bugs in Postgres, such as this numerical bug that can cause valid SP-GiST operations to fail , this format cache bug that can cause incorrect results from JSONPath , this pgcrypto bug that can cause later operations to fail , multiple memory safety bugs in the dictionary loader 2 , this money overflow bug , etc.

This isn't to say that pgrust is bug free 3 , but it does indicate that there's a substantial amount of testing happening and, even if pgrust itself is never successful, just making the attempt will have improved Postgres in a durable way. The main pitch for pgrust is actually performance, and that's where the really interesting work is happening; if pgrust fails, it's possible that some of the optimizations they've demonstrated will make it into Postgres, Clickhouse, etc., but that's obviously less direct than filing Postgres bugs which get fixed.

That being said, I find it understandable that, every time I see pgrust discussed on a news aggregator, most people dismiss it as vibeslop garbage because almost all of these rewrite projects are slop. If I didn't know Malis, I would make the same assumption, because who has the time to look into all of these projects? Because I know Malis, I didn't bother to look at it; I just trusted him (I only found the above because I wanted to check on pgrust before using it as an example for this post).

As a consumer of software, everywhere you look, there's slow software that the creator is claiming is fast because the creator is touting some slop benchmark, e.g., here's one of multiple examples I saw yesterday , and of course low-quality software that doesn't work is more common than ever.

But, as a builder of software, it doesn't matter that almost all of these projects are vibeslop, that other people are out there shoveling out huge piles of crap and calling it gold . You can build things like pgrust or other projects that would've been too large to really be feasible in the past and, if you do a reasonable job with testing and benchmarking, that stuff can actually be good-enough quality to use.

If I were writing it, I would say "we can be more ambitious with the software we build" and not "we should", but Malis has been casually chatting with me when he's said this, so maybe he would say the same in an actual post; don't read too much into should vs. can here. What's interesting to me is how capabilities have advanced such that we can do a lot more.

Just for example, after hearing that OpenAI was going to use Cerebras for their SOTA models and not just fast-but-low-quality models like 5.3-Codex-Spark, I looked at where time on my computer would go if I was using a SOTA model, but 10x to 100x faster; some things that were already sometimes a bottleneck that would only get worse with a faster model were:

At the level of a "works for me" project, these are all things that can seriously be improved. I don't have much spare time at the moment but, even so, I built this regex engine that can be tweaked to be faster than other general-purpose regex libraries on any particular workload I care about , this ripgrep fork that uses the native code compiler from the regex engine and is faster for my codex ripgrep workloads (of course a text index is the better solution, but I've already worked on text indexing and this was a "just for fun" project where I wasn't trying to do the optimal thing), and a Rust that sped up builds for my projects (huge improvement for cold builds, moderate for warm, limited by wanting to avoid forking the Rust compiler front-end). For syscalls and filesystem overhead, just switching development from Mac to Linux improved this a lot, and of course this is another thing that can be sped up a lot as well, especially when agents are hammering lots of small filesystem operations (it's not uncommon to see my machine waiting on filesystem ops because the standard OS filesystem interface wasn't designed with modern disk performance in mind). With modern disks, there's no reason to use the *nix filesystem API. In the past, writing a developer toolchain that uses direct I/O instead of normal filessytem operations or building a custom OS or a funny layer that fakes out syscalls would've been an absurd endevaor, but that's totally doable now.

For someone like me who doesn't know anything about regexes, string matching algorithms, compilers, interpreters, etc., this set of projects would've taken a year or more to get to "works for me" quality. Instead, this was a low single-digit number of hours of my time. If I wanted to make any of these things meet a "useful product or open source project" quality bar, that would be a lot more work 0 , but it's still pretty incredible how much this process is sped up.

My read of Malis's meaning when he says “we should be more ambitious with the software we build”, is that it doesn't even occur to people to do these things that are now easy. For weeks, every time I logged into Twitter, I saw someone complain about how Rust compilation is slow and is limiting development velocity (I think this wasn't actually true when I saw the complaints, in that this was before 5.6 Sol and 6 Astra were available on Cerebras, and if you measured where the time actually went, Rust compilation time wasn't actually that much of a bottleneck at the time). Sure, Rust compliation is slow. You can just write a Rust interpreter as well as speed up compilation directly. There are problems like this which I see people complaining about daily that are solvable without a lot of time or effort now. As far as I can tell, these problems are problems because people are implicitly carrying around a pre-agentic cost model. Ten years ago, the kind of person who implemented a new compiler because their compiler was slow was the kind of person who started programming a new 3d game engine when they wanted to make an indie game, i.e., the kind of person who never ships anything. Most productive programmers I know still have an aversion to this kind of thing, even though it is now actually reasonable to implement this kind of thing now 4 .

Another project I previously mentioned was this Azul AI which is superhuman at matched time controls . When I did that (with GPT-5.1/5.2), with zero AI knowledge, it took about 5 hours of my time to get something superhuman, and about 20 hours of my time to become what appeared to be the strongest AI at the time, including being stronger against humans than this AI that was used to cheat on Board Game Arena . Gabriel Cangussu recently built an AI that demolishes my AI, and AFAICT, it took him substantially less time than my AI took me. From talking to him about it, one key difference is that Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5 have a much better understanding of board game AIs. When I used GPT-5.1/5.2, pretty much every suggestion they had was wrong and I had to do a lot of steering to get things to be remotely reasonable. If I had GPT read a codebase or a paper to implement relevant techniques from the paper, it would fail. If I read the paper myself and named a technique, it would say it did the technique, but it would generally do something that superficially looked like the technique but wasn't the actual technique until I issued some corrections. When the model is that far from being able to do the right thing, if you have no background in the area, it's fairly time consuming to check if the model did the right thing since you have to learn enough about what it's supposed to do to be able to check that it did what was claimed.

When I did that project, I said to friends that I didn't think the state models were in could last. It seemed impossible that they wouldn't get good enough to be able to read a paper and implement the techniques soon, and it seemed like they should also be able to pick out codebases and papers to crib from as well. From my experience messing around a bit with Fable 5 and Cangussu's experience with Fable 5.1 and Opus 5.5, that seems to have happened, which is a huge time saver for someone like me who doesn't know anything about board game AIs (I know a little bit now, but still less than any real AI researcher) 5 .

For any particular domain, like board game AIs, you can say, "who cares? Board game AIs don't matter", but I've found this increase in capability to be true in quite a few different domains. Just for example, I did this toy eval of verification and test techniques with GPT-5.6 Sol implementing zstd on medium and xhigh . I haven't had time to write it up, but when I published that post, I also re-did the evals with GPT-6 Astra. 6 Astra was so good that I had to find different evals because models had advanced too much. For zstd, 6 Astra succeeds at passing all of the registered tests more than 99% of the time across all conditions, even the ones that significantly impair performance, like using TDD (and, BTW, it does it more cheaply as well, taking about $1 to implement zstd). I ended up using the IMAP RFC, which 5.6 Sol couldn't do effectively, and Pandoc, which is a pretty major thing to implement as it needs to be able to read and write many different formats 6 .
